body:
These read-only APIs qualify saved automation history during application replacement. A receipt proves exact immutable history, never a live provider or permission to bypass source ownership. This Draft adds archived-pane and completed-pane inspection without opening a service, migrating the source database, or starting a provider. No production archive caller is wired at this head.

The corrections bound borrowed workspace-key and kind-tag bytes before String conversion, require a retained terminal’s nested relaunch recipe to match its originally issued console launch, and count transcript metadata using the parsed canonical terminal ID that the existing loader consumes. Accepted UUID aliases remain accepted. The shared terminal-byte inspection also corrects main’s inherited raw-key aggregate undercharge: each window reserves actual canonical descriptor bytes before decoding, across the existing whole-inventory budget. The raw-ID String preflight is limited by both the 4 MiB descriptor ceiling and the remaining aggregate allowance. Main’s future-schema refusal, historical provenance selection, schema-aware loader, row/deadline limits, read-only transaction and retained-source decisions remain intact. This bounds the specified Rust copies, not SQLite internals or total process memory.

Regression source covers both real inspectors, exact-key poison claims, byte/UTF-8/type boundaries, all five nested LaunchRecipe fields, legitimate ended consoles and raw normalized continuity changes. Canonical path versus raw-key decoy cases preserve bounded positives and inclusive limits. A new real-StateStore fixture spans two windows with two descriptors each, uses valid canonical transcript foreign-key parents, and derives its expected byte charge independently from serialized fixture values. It checks exact aggregate admission, one-byte-short refusal and inventory refusal before malformed JSON decoding. Source-byte comparisons check read-only behavior; these assertions do not measure allocations or qualify whole-source admission.

Current source `4fa3370532d78d8e19099639f2bc40c711dc725a`, tree `ea6671347bb1c2aa84f240f9b4727c00346403bc`, includes a normal ancestry-preserving merge of main `e8842819519dff74c0726d1fdd94f435b495a153`. Only `src/automations.rs`, `src/automations/archive.rs` and `src/persistence.rs` differ from that main; general terminal loader and continuity restoration are unchanged. Separate nonauthor production/schema and regression-oracle source reviews are recorded below. Official Rust 1.93 `scripts/check-format` and whitespace checks pass at this source. **Compilation and every new or modified regression remain UNRUN**, pending the serial validation queue.

The earlier Script contracts run [41078804359](https://github.com/CarsonBurke/cagents/actions/runs/41078804359/job/124142095639) failed at source-file verification because historical `015e222` lacked four current formatter/runner files. It did not run meaningful product tests. Current-main composition restores those files without changing the gate; The exact current-head [Script contracts run 41084001631](https://github.com/CarsonBurke/cagents/actions/runs/41084001631/job/124160232059) passed. Source review also caught a missing canonical foreign-key parent in the first new fixture and duplicate helpers in the clean textual merge. Both source negatives are preserved and corrected; neither is claimed as an executed runtime/compiler result.

Independent source review found no blocker in the exact `4fa33705` production accounting/schema preservation or the new multiwindow oracle. The unchanged archived-console recipe guard was separately reviewed at `60e81479`; its normalized-row oracle was corrected at `afa06ba7` after the foreign-key finding. These are source reviews only. Compilation, tests and native execution remain unqualified.

Remaining gates: separate affected HOST and UI compilation and owning regressions; broader isolated-suite conservation; whole-inventory/admission and actual replacement integration. Archive readiness remains downstream of managed-proof and WHOLE-scope admission before SeedView. No upgrade exemption, native qualification, installed-product progress or merge readiness is claimed. Keep Draft.
